title: Kill shared local admin passwords with Windows LAPS (Entra ID or AD)
summary: When every device has the same local administrator password, one stolen hash opens them all. Windows LAPS, built into Windows, rotates a unique password per device and backs it up to Microsoft Entra ID or Active Directory. It's free, and the legacy Microsoft LAPS is deprecated.
steps: Entra ID: first enable LAPS at tenant level in the Microsoft Entra device settings. Microsoft Entra ID doesn't accept LAPS passwords until you do.
Deploy policy. For Entra-joined devices Microsoft prefers Intune with the Windows LAPS CSP; hybrid devices can use Windows LAPS Group Policy. For Entra ID, set at minimum BackupDirectory = 1.

Leave AdministratorAccountName empty to manage the built-in administrator, which LAPS finds by its well-known RID. If you set a custom account name, create that account yourself (for example with the Accounts CSP), because LAPS doesn't create it.
Test on a device: `Invoke-LapsPolicyProcessing`, then look for Event 10029 (password backed up to Entra ID).

Retrieve passwords through the Entra or Intune portal, or with `Get-LapsAADPassword -DeviceIds <device> -IncludePasswords` (Entra) or `Get-LapsADPassword` (AD). Force a rotation after use with `Reset-LapsPassword`.

AD mode: extend the schema with `Update-LapsADSchema`, let computers write their own password with `Set-LapsADComputerSelfPermission`, and check who can read passwords with `Find-LapsADExtendedRights`.
pitfalls: The built-in Entra roles that can read LAPS passwords are highly privileged, so review who holds them.
A device backs up to Entra ID or to AD, never both. Workplace-joined (registered) devices aren't supported.
Legacy LAPS emulation mode stores passwords in AD in clear text, so treat it only as a migration step.
Avoid running Reset-LapsPassword too often, because Entra ID may throttle it.
Windows LAPS is free; Entra ID backup works with Microsoft Entra ID Free or higher. The Automatic Account Management settings need Windows 11 24H2 or Server 2025.
